advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Only overwrite REVIEWBOT_WEBHOOK_AUTH_OFFSET_FILE when the review-bot health body was actually parsed, so a transient unreachable probe cannot zero the offset and cause double-counting on recovery.
evidence: review_webhook_auth_rejections=0 (line 185) is the value used when `review_body` is empty (bot unreachable)
The `if [ -n "$review_body" ]` block (line 186) only updates rejections when the body is present; otherwise it stays 0
`printf '%s\n' "$review_webhook_auth_rejections" >"$REVIEWBOT_WEBHOOK_AUTH_OFFSET_FILE"` (line 230) runs unconditionally, so a probe-failure interval clobbers the offset to 0
On recovery `[ "$review_webhook_auth_rejections" -ge "$review_webhook_auth_prev" ]` is true (N >= 0) → delta=N re-published
advisory.finding: In observability.sh, a transient review-bot probe failure (unreachable → empty body) leaves review_webhook_auth_rejections=0 but STILL unconditionally overwrites the offset file with 0 (line 230). When the bot recovers on a later interval with its process-local counter still at N (no restart occurred), the code computes delta = N - 0 = N and re-publishes N rejections that were already published/counted in a prior window, producing a spurious page for the reviewbot-webhook-auth-rejections alarm.
advisory.suggested_fix: Guard the offset write (and delta computation) so it runs only inside the `if [ -n "$review_body" ]` success path; on an unreachable probe, leave the offset untouched and publish delta 0.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the health-payload parser emit a distinguishable failure token (not "0 0") so observability.sh can tell 'checked and clean' from 'instrument failed' before publishing a 0 rejection delta.
evidence: `' "$review_body" 2>/dev/null || echo 0` (line 208) — a total python3 failure falls back to the bare string "0"
`review_webhook_auth_rejections="${review_payload##* }"` (line 211) then extracts "0" from that single token
`except: print("0 0")` inside the parser also maps malformed JSON to zero rejections
No assertion that the parser produced the expected two-token output before trusting the rejection count
advisory.finding: observability.sh cannot distinguish 'review-bot reports zero rejections' from 'the JSON instrument failed / received wrong input'. When python3 is missing or errors, `|| echo 0` yields review_payload="0", so review_webhook_auth_rejections parses to 0 and delta is 0 — the rejection signal silently reports clean even though the parse never actually ran against a real payload.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Distinguish a transient Gerrit-host name-resolution failure (socket.gaierror) from a genuine stale-token/unauthorized rejection so it is not counted into `webhook_auth_rejections` and mis-paged by the stale-token rotation alarm.
evidence: Primary (transient) failure: `_resolve_host_addresses` catches `socket.gaierror` and returns `set()` — src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:218-219 (`except socket.gaierror:` / `return set()`).

Downgrade site: `_is_internal_gerrit_webhook` gates internal acceptance on `client_host in _configured_gerrit_service_addresses(cfg)` (src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:247); an empty set from a DNS blip forces this False regardless of a legitimate Gerrit peer.

Old surfaced disposition: internal-delivery acceptance previously depended on the URL/header token compare (`hmac.compare_digest(token, cfg.webhook_token)`), which never consulted DNS — a name-resolution blip could not produce an auth rejection. New: same blip yields 401 via `if not _webhook_authorized(request, cfg):` (src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:654-657).

Secondary/fallback failure recorded: `_record_webhook_auth_rejection(request.app)` increments `webhook_auth_rejections` (src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:263-266, 655), surfaced on /health via `_webhook_auth_rejection_health` (src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:269-277, 615-635).

Classifier that changes behavior: observability.sh publishes `reviewbot_webhook_auth_rejections` from the health payload (infra/scripts/observability.sh new put_metric_data block) and the alarm `rebar-reviewbot-webhook-auth-rejections` in infra/terraform/monitoring_autodeploy.tf declares the cause as 'missing or stale X-Rebar-Token' with remediation 'check infra/gerrit/service-user.sh rotation output ... restart or reload Gerrit/webhooks so the plugin uses the current token' — i.e. a transient DNS fault is classified/paged as a permanent token-rotation failure.
advisory.finding: A transient DNS/name-resolution failure resolving the Gerrit service host is swallowed to an empty address set and masked as a permanent webhook-auth rejection, which the CloudWatch classifier attributes to a stale/missing token rather than a transient dependency fault.
advisory.suggested_fix: Propagate/branch on the DNS failure separately: when `_configured_gerrit_service_addresses` cannot resolve the Gerrit host (gaierror), log/emit a distinct transient-resolution signal (or fail-open the internal path guarded by the X-Forwarded-For check) instead of returning False and incrementing the auth-rejection counter, so the stale-token alarm classifier only fires on real token faults.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the tokenless internal webhook path's reliance on peer-IP + client-controlled headers is an acceptable authorization gate vs. requiring a non-forgeable credential.
evidence: `_is_internal_gerrit_webhook` returns True on `bool(origin) and origin in expected_origins and not forwarded_for and client_host in _configured_gerrit_service_addresses(cfg)` (app.py:243-248) — X-Origin-Url and X-Forwarded-For are client-controlled; only client_host is non-forgeable
`_webhook_authorized` falls back to `_is_internal_gerrit_webhook` when the token compare fails (app.py:251-255), so no shared secret is required on that path

docker-compose.yml comment: 'the receiver accepts that header only from the resolved compose-network Gerrit service peer' (docker-compose.yml:140-142) — confirms the design intent that source IP is the gate

ADR-0014 documents this as a deliberate token->network-boundary reduction ('a header the plugin actually sends instead of a `header =` config key it ignores, without trusting that client-controlled header by itself')
advisory.finding: The Gerrit->review-bot internal webhook path now accepts tokenless requests: authorization reduces to the TCP peer IP resolving to the Gerrit service host plus two client-controlled headers (X-Origin-Url match, X-Forwarded-For absent). The only non-forgeable factor is the source IP on the shared docker-compose bridge, so any workload that can originate a connection from (or occupy) Gerrit's bridge IP reaches an authenticated sink (enqueue -> clone change ref -> cast LLM-Review vote) with no secret.
scenarios: A second/future container on the compose network sharing or spoofing Gerrit's bridge IP posts to review-bot:8000/webhook with a forged X-Origin-Url and no X-Forwarded-For, and is accepted tokenless.
Gerrit container compromise yields direct authenticated webhook injection with no additional credential.

evidence: src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:236-248 `origin = request.headers.get("X-Origin-Url", "")...return (bool(origin) and origin in expected_origins and not forwarded_for and client_host in _configured_gerrit_service_addresses(cfg))`
src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:232-234 docstring: `The header is not a secret, so it is only accepted when the TCP peer resolves to the configured Gerrit service host.`

The only cryptographic credential (webhook_token) is bypassed entirely for this path (_webhook_authorized L251-255 falls through to _is_internal_gerrit_webhook); the residual gate is a network-identity assertion, so the trust boundary is the compose network's peer-IP integrity, not a secret.
src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:233 docstring: `Public nginx requests always carry X-Forwarded-For, so absence of that header is the final guard that keeps this fallback off the public edge.`
src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:237,246 `forwarded_for = request.headers.get("X-Forwarded-For", "").strip()` ... `and not forwarded_for`

infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template:70 `proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;` — the invariant lives in a separate, independently-editable config file, so auth correctness is coupled across a trust boundary.
advisory.finding: The internal-webhook auth bypass accepts tokenless POST /webhook requests based only on a client-controlled X-Origin-Url header plus a TCP-peer-IP check against the resolved Gerrit service address; any workload on the shared docker compose network that resolves to (or acquires, via container-restart IP reuse) the Gerrit service IP can forge the non-secret X-Origin-Url and submit tokenless webhooks that enqueue LLM-Review work.

evidence: observability.sh:230-231 `printf '%s\n' "$review_webhook_auth_rejections" >"$REVIEWBOT_WEBHOOK_AUTH_OFFSET_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true` — offset written before/independent of publish success

Ticket 073f AC: 'observability.sh publishes a per-interval reviewbot_webhook_auth_rejections metric without losing increments across review-bot restarts or failed CloudWatch publishes'

observability.sh:184 `review_ok=0; [ "$review_code" = "200" ] && review_ok=1` and :186 `if [ -n "$review_body" ]` — on probe failure review_body is empty so the payload parse block is skipped and review_webhook_auth_rejections stays 0

observability.sh:172 `review_probe=... || printf '\n000'` — failed probe yields empty body
advisory.finding: observability.sh advances/persists the webhook-auth offset file unconditionally, even when the CloudWatch `put_metric_data` publish fails. Because the publish is guarded by `2>/dev/null || true`, a failed publish still leaves the offset written to the current sampled value, so the un-published rejection increments are lost on the next window — the counter never re-emits them.
advisory.suggested_fix: Capture the put_metric_data exit status for the rejections metric and only write $REVIEWBOT_WEBHOOK_AUTH_OFFSET_FILE when it returned 0.

advisory.finding: The internal Gerrit webhook path is authenticated only by a client-controlled header (X-Origin-Url) plus TCP-peer-IP resolution and absence of X-Forwarded-For; because the review-bot compose service declares no `networks:` block, every sibling compose container shares the default bridge and can reach review-bot:8000, so the blast radius of the tokenless accept path is any container that can present the Gerrit service peer IP.

evidence: app.py:233-234 `Public nginx requests always carry ``X-Forwarded-For``, so absence of that header is the final guard that keeps this fallback off the public edge.`
app.py:243-248 the return also requires `client_host in _configured_gerrit_service_addresses(cfg)`, which is the actual non-forgeable gate

advisory.finding: The docstring and comments claim absence of X-Forwarded-For is 'the final guard that keeps this fallback off the public edge', but X-Forwarded-For is client-controllable and is NOT the real gate — the peer-address membership check is. A public request that reached the receiver without X-Forwarded-For (e.g. an nginx misconfig or a future direct-exposure change) would still be rejected only by the peer check, not by the XFF absence. The comment overstates a client header's protective role.
